blocks.text: Kitchen or Bathroom: Painting Cabinets Without Breaking the Bank

When it comes to updating your kitchen or bathroom, one of the biggest design decisions is choosing between painting your existing cabinets or replacing them entirely. Both options have their pros and cons, and the choice often depends on your budget, timeline, and desired style. With the right colors and finishes, painting cabinets can give your space a fresh, modern look, sometimes even better than brand-new cabinetry.
At Black Pearl Painters, we help homeowners make informed decisions and bring their vision to life with professional cabinet painting services using premium paints like Sherwin-Williams.
Why Painting Cabinets Can Be a Smart Choice
1. Cost-Effective Transformation
Replacing cabinets is expensive, often involving custom orders, demolition, and installation. Painting cabinets is far more budget-friendly, often costing a fraction of a full replacement.
2. Less Disruption
A full kitchen or bathroom remodel can take weeks. Professional painting is faster and less invasive, letting you continue using your space with minimal downtime.
3. Customization and Flexibility
Painting allows you to experiment with trending colors and finishes without committing to permanent cabinetry. You can choose matte, satin, or semi-gloss finishes to suit your style.
4. Eco-Friendly Option
Instead of discarding perfectly good cabinets, painting keeps them in use and reduces waste — making it a more sustainable choice.
When Replacement Makes Sense
While painting cabinets is cost-effective, there are times when replacing cabinets is the better option:

items: Cabinets are structurally damaged (warped, water-damaged, or broken).
You want to change the layout of your kitchen or bathroom.
You desire a completely new style or custom features that painting alone can’t achieve.

blocks.text: In most cases, if the cabinet boxes are in good condition, painting is an excellent way to update your space without the cost and hassle of full replacement.

blocks.alt: painting cabinets, painting vs replacing transforming cabinets
blocks.title: Painting Cabinets Vs. Replacing: Transform Your Kitchen Or Bathroom Without Breaking The Bank

blocks.text: Trending Cabinet Colors for 2025
Color trends play a huge role in modernizing your cabinets. Choosing the right hue can make a small kitchen feel spacious or add luxury to a bathroom. Here’s what’s trending:
1. Neutral and Warm Tones

items: Greige: A blend of gray and beige, perfect for kitchens and bathrooms seeking a calm, timeless aesthetic.
Creamy White or Off-White: Keeps spaces feeling bright and clean, while offering versatility for hardware and countertop choices.
Taupe or Soft Brown: Adds warmth to kitchens with wood or stone accents.

blocks.text: Best For: Entire kitchen cabinets or bathroom vanities, especially when paired with a contrasting island.
2. Moody and Deep Hues

items: Navy Blue: Popular for lower cabinets or islands, creating a modern, grounded look.
Charcoal or Slate Gray: Adds drama and elegance without overwhelming the space.
Forest Green: Ideal for accent cabinets or a statement kitchen island, evoking a nature-inspired, sophisticated feel.

blocks.text: Best For: Kitchen islands, lower cabinets, or accent walls in bathrooms.
3. Light and Airy Pastels

items: Soft Sage Green: Calming and versatile, works well in bathrooms and kitchens.
Pale Blue or Aqua: Adds a pop of color while keeping a serene, coastal vibe.
Blush or Mauve: Trending for modern bathrooms and transitional kitchens, giving a subtle warmth.

blocks.text: Best For: Upper cabinets, small islands, or bathroom vanities to create a fresh, inviting feel.
4. Two-Tone Cabinets
A growing trend is mixing colors for upper and lower cabinets, such as:

items: Upper cabinets in Soft White or Sunbleached, lower cabinets in Navy Blue or Charcoal.
Kitchen islands in a bold accent color like Forest Green or Mauve, with surrounding cabinets in neutral tones.

blocks.text: This approach adds visual interest and depth without overwhelming the space.
Benefits of Professional Cabinet Painting
While DIY painting is possible, professional painters bring precision and durability that make a huge difference:

items: Surface Prep: Proper sanding, cleaning, and priming prevent peeling, bubbling, or uneven finish.
Durable Finishes: High-quality paints like Sherwin-Williams Emerald Urethane or ProClassic create smooth, hard-wearing surfaces that withstand kitchen and bathroom wear and tear.
Hardware and Detail Work: Professionals ensure edges, trim, and corners are flawless, giving cabinets a “like-new” appearance.

blocks.text: With professional painting, your cabinets can look custom, refreshed, and modern — all without replacing a single door.

blocks.title: Painting Cabinets Vs. Replacing: Transform Your Kitchen Or Bathroom Without Breaking The Bank

blocks.text: Considerations for Kitchen Islands
Kitchen islands are often the focal point of your space. Painting or updating your island can dramatically change the room’s aesthetic:

items: Moody Hues: Navy, charcoal, or deep green create a luxurious contrast to lighter perimeter cabinets.
Bold Accent Colors: Mustard, teal, or even black islands are trending for modern and transitional kitchens.
Two-Tone Harmony: Pair your island color with neutral cabinetry to create depth and dimension.

blocks.text: Professional painters can ensure your island color matches the style of the room while standing out as a centerpiece.
Trending Bathroom Cabinet Colors
Bathroom vanities are also embracing color trends. Popular options include:

items: Soft Gray or Greige: Timeless and versatile, works well with marble or quartz countertops.
Sage or Muted Green: Creates a spa-like, calming environment.
Deep Navy or Charcoal: Adds elegance and contrast for modern bathrooms.
Two-Tone Vanities: Combining a bold lower cabinet with lighter upper cabinets or open shelving.

blocks.text: Even small changes, like painting vanity doors or drawer fronts, can elevate the space without full replacement.
Final Thoughts: Painting vs. Replacing
Choosing between painting and replacing your cabinets depends on:

items: Condition: Good cabinets? Painting works beautifully. Damaged or outdated layout? Consider replacement.
Budget: Painting is more cost-effective and eco-friendly.
Style Goals: Want to experiment with trendy colors or two-tone designs? Painting offers flexibility.
Timeframe: Painting is faster and less disruptive than replacement.

blocks.text: With the right colors and professional application, painting cabinets is often the smartest choice for homeowners looking to modernize kitchens and bathrooms without the cost and hassle of a full remodel.

blocks.text: Bold Trends that Transform your Home: Our Specialty

At Black Pearl Painters, we believe painting is more than just refreshing walls—it’s about shaping mood, character, and identity in every room. As interior paint trends evolve, homeowners and designers alike are turning to immersive, expressive techniques. One of the the most talked-about trends for 2025 is color drenching, and it’s redefining how we think about walls, ceilings, and trim. In this post, we’ll explore color drenching and other new interior paint trends, spotlight Sherwin-Williams paints, and offer tips for turning your home into a design-forward haven.
What Is Color Drenching, and Why It’s Trending

“Color drenching” refers to the technique of applying a single hue (or a very limited palette) across all surfaces in a room, walls, ceiling, trim, and sometimes even doors and built-ins. The goal is a cohesive, immersive environment where color flows seamlessly. It rejects the old norm of white ceilings or contrasting trim, opting instead to wrap the room in unified tone and feeling.
Designers are embracing color drenching because it:

items: Creates bold, dramatic impact in even modest spaces
Helps mask imperfections or transitions between wall and ceiling
Evens out visual attention so furniture and artwork can pop
Gives a sense of intimacy and continuity to a room

blocks.text: That said, pulling it off well requires finesse. Lighting, undertones, finish selection, and balance with furnishings are all critical.
Pro Tips for Successful Color Drenching

items: Skip white ceilings — the hallmark of true drenching is extending color overhead.
Watch lighting and undertones — a hue may shift under different light; test swatches throughout the day.
Consider finish contrast — use flatter finishes on walls and slightly glossier sheens on trim or doors to subtly separate planes.
Use “double drenching” — pick a lighter shade for the ceiling and a deeper one for walls to balance height and flow.
Balance it with texture — when everything shares hue, layering texture (wood, textiles, metal) becomes essential to avoid flatness

blocks.text: Color drenching is turning many rooms into enveloping art pieces—and when done with quality paints (like those from Sherwin-Williams), the effect can last beautifully.

blocks.alt: color drenching, interior color trends, bold colors
blocks.title: Welcome To The Next Era Of Interior Color: Bold Trends That Transform Spaces

blocks.text: Other Interior Paint Trends to Watch in 2025
While color drenching dominates conversations, several companion trends are shaping interior painting in 2025:
1. Organic Neutrals with Warmth

Gone are the days of stark greys and icy neutrals. The trend now leans toward earthy, warm neutrals that feel grounding and welcoming. Sherwin-Williams’ 2025 Color Capsule of the Year features tones like Grounded SW 6089 (a rich earthen brown) and Bosc Pear SW 6390 (a golden organic hue) to reflect this shift.
These soothing neutrals play beautifully in drench schemes or as anchor tones to mix with more saturated accents.
2. Quiet Accent Colors & Depth Hues

Accent pops are moving toward deeper, more sophisticated shades—muted mauves, moody blues, stormy greys. Sherwin-Williams’ forecast includes Rain Cloud SW 9639 and Mauve Finery SW 6282 in its 2025 capsule.
In a drench context, these can anchor focal walls, ceiling accents, or transitions between adjoining rooms.
3. Color Drift & Painterly Blends

Some designers are softening the edges of monochrome by subtly blending adjacent tones into walls, creating softened gradients or drift-like transitions. This gives visual interest without harsh shifts. (Sherwin-Williams’ Colormix® forecast acknowledges evolving palettes and motion in color.)
4. Strong Statement Ceilings

Even outside of full drenching, bold ceilings are making a comeback. Instead of defaulting to white, designers are choosing saturated ceiling hues to add drama and reduce the visual break between wall and ceiling. This ties into drenching principles.
5. Layered Texture and Sheens

With strong color choices, texture is more important than ever. Expect to see finishes like matte, eggshell, and satin used in juxtaposition, wall treatments (veneer, plaster, textural paints), and tactile materials integrated with paint for depth.

blocks.text: Why Sherwin-Williams Paints Make the Difference
When it comes to executing color-forward schemes like drenching, Sherwin-Williams stands out for several reasons:

items: Their Color Technology and color forecasting (Colormix®, Color Capsule of the Year) help you stay on trend while maintaining cohesion.
Their Top 50 Colors collection offers go-to, balanced hues—like Agreeable Gray or Natural Linen—which can anchor dramatic schemes.
They offer specialty lines (Emerald, Duration, etc.) known for durability, washability, and color retention—essential when you want immersive color everywhere.
Their tools, like peel-and-stick samples or color visualization, let homeowners preview bold drench schemes risk-free.

blocks.text: By partnering with Sherwin-Williams paints, Black Pearl Painters ensures your bold color visions are backed with performance and accuracy.
How Black Pearl Painters Can Help Bring These Trends to Life
At Black Pearl Painters, we don’t just roll on paint; we craft environments. Here’s how we support clients who want to ride the wave of new interior paint trends:

items: Surface Prep & ExecutionDrenching demands consistent coverage. Our professional prep (priming, smoothing, caulking) ensures no patchiness or bleed-through cracks color fidelity.
Finish DifferentiationEven in drench schemes, we use subtle variation in sheen (satin trims, eggshell walls) to bring depth and dimension while staying cohesive.

Long-Term Maintenance AdviceBecause drenching covers more surfaces, we help choose the right Sherwin-Williams formulas (washable, low-VOC, high durability) to keep your interiors looking fresh for years.

blocks.text: Final Thoughts

Interior design is finally moving past restrained neutrals and slaps of accent paint. Color drenching is liberating interiors from contrast conventions and creating immersive, soulful environments. Pairing this bold technique with palette direction from Sherwin-Williams ensures both aesthetic and technical excellence.

If you’re dreaming of transforming your home with dramatic, modern paint, drenching ceilings, walls, and trim in unified tones, Black Pearl Painters has the creative vision and execution expertise to bring it to life. blocks.text: Your Interior Paint Sheen Guide from Black Pearl Painters

When planning your next interior painting project in Tacoma, Bonney Lake, or the greater Puget Sound area, one of the most overlooked decisions is choosing the right paint finish; also known as paint sheen. Our paint sheen guide demonstrates while color takes center stage, the finish you select can dramatically affect the look, feel, and durability of your painted walls.

At Black Pearl Painters, we often help clients decide between eggshell, satin, and semi-gloss finishes, especially when painting living rooms, bedrooms, kitchens, and trim. These three sheens offer different benefits in terms of appearance, cleanability, and resistance to wear and the wrong choice can impact how your walls age over time.
This guide breaks down everything you need to know to confidently select the best interior paint finish for your space, room by room.
Understanding Our Paint Sheen Guide: What Does It Mean?
Paint sheen refers to the amount of light a painted surface reflects. The more reflective the surface, the shinier and more durable the paint tends to be. Sheens typically fall along a spectrum:

items: Flat / Matte – No shine, great for hiding imperfections
Gloss / High Gloss – Very shiny, almost lacquer-like

blocks.text: For most interior walls, the top three contenders are eggshell, satin, and semi-gloss; each offering a balance between beauty and performance.

blocks.alt: paint sheen guide, paint sheen, paint finishes
blocks.title: Paint Sheen Guide: How To Choose Eggshell, Satin, Or Semi-Gloss

blocks.text: Eggshell Finish: Subtle, Soft, and Stylish
Eggshell paint finish has a very slight sheen; just enough to give walls a velvety smooth appearance without being shiny.
Best For:
Pros:

items: Hides imperfections well, making it great for older homes or walls with minor dents
Easier to clean than flat paint (though not as washable as satin)

blocks.text: Cons:

items: Not ideal for high-moisture areas or walls that get constant contact (like near doors or light switches)
May show scuffing over time in high-traffic zones

blocks.text: Black Pearl Pro Tip:

If you love a soft, elegant look and don’t need extreme washability, eggshell is a great go-to for many interior walls. In homes with kids or pets, use it in lower-touch spaces like guest rooms or living rooms with minimal traffic.
Satin Finish: The Balanced All-Around Performer

Satin paint finish is a crowd favorite for good reason; it strikes the perfect balance between durability and appearance. With a subtle sheen that reflects more light than eggshell, satin adds depth and dimension to walls while offering enhanced scrubbability.
Best For:
Pros:

items: Resists moisture better than lower sheens
Gives a warm, inviting glow without looking glossy

blocks.text: Cons:

items: Slightly more reflective, so wall flaws may be more noticeable
Requires careful application to avoid lap marks or roller streaks

blocks.text: Black Pearl Pro Tip:

Satin is often the best paint finish for interior walls in active households. If you’re repainting a busy hallway, kid’s room, or high-traffic living space in Bonney Lake or Tacoma, satin is likely your best bet.
Semi-Gloss Finish: Durable and Easy to Clean

Semi-gloss paint has a shiny, smooth finish that reflects light and stands up to tough conditions. It’s typically reserved for high-moisture areas or surfaces that get touched frequently, such as trim, doors, and cabinetry.
Best For:
Pros:

items: Moisture-resistant, making it perfect for bathrooms or kitchens
Creates contrast when paired with lower-sheen wall finishes (great for trim)

blocks.text: Cons:

items: Shiny surface shows flaws—requires careful surface prep
Can feel too glossy for full walls unless strategically used

blocks.text: Black Pearl Pro Tip:

We recommend semi-gloss primarily for accent features and areas that need frequent cleaning. For bathrooms or laundry rooms, it provides excellent water resistance, but make sure your walls are smooth and well-prepped for best results.
Paint Sheen Guide: A Quick Breakdown
Tips for Choosing the Right Sheen
1. Match Sheen to Room Function
Think about how each room is used. If it sees lots of traffic, use satin. If it’s mainly decorative, eggshell may be just fine. And for damp or wipe-prone areas, semi-gloss is your best friend.
2. Think About Light
Glossy finishes reflect more light and can highlight imperfections. In rooms with large windows or strong overhead lighting, satin or eggshell will feel more natural and forgiving.
3. Pair Sheens for Visual Contrast
Using semi-gloss on trim and eggshell or satin on walls adds contrast and makes architectural details pop. This is a classic approach in both modern and traditional home design.
4. Consider Paint Quality

Higher-end paints like Sherwin-Williams Emerald® or Duration® Home offer better performance regardless of sheen. These products are more washable and apply more smoothly—an essential factor when choosing sheens like satin or semi-gloss.

blocks.title: Paint Sheen Guide: How To Choose Eggshell, Satin, Or Semi-Gloss

blocks.text: Why Paint Finish Choice Matters in the Pacific Northwest
In the moist, cool climate of Tacoma and the surrounding Puget Sound, your paint needs to work hard, especially in areas like bathrooms, laundry rooms, and kitchens where condensation is common.
Choosing the right paint finish means you’ll enjoy:

items: Walls that resist mildew and moisture
More visually cohesive interiors that reflect your home’s character

blocks.text: Fall Painting: 8 Reasons Why it is the Perfect Season for Interior Painting!

When the leaves start to change, many homeowners focus on cozying up their spaces for the cooler months ahead. While fall is known for pumpkin spice lattes, crisp air, and holiday prep, it’s also one of the best times of year for home improvement projects, especially interior painting. If you’ve been thinking about giving your living room a fresh coat of paint, sprucing up the dining room before guests arrive, or finally tackling the bedrooms, fall offers unique advantages. Black Pearl Painters is here to break down why fall is an ideal season for interior painting, plus provide tips to make your project smooth, efficient, and long-lasting.
1. Ideal Fall Painting Conditions Indoors

Even though you’re painting inside, weather still plays a role. In fall, the humidity levels drop, and temperatures are moderate—two factors that impact paint’s ability to cure properly. Paint dries too quickly in summer heat, and winter cold can prevent proper adhesion. Fall strikes a balance, giving you the perfect conditions for a smooth, even finish.
2. Prepping for the Holidays

Fall is often the gateway to the busiest season of the year; holiday gatherings, family visits, and festive celebrations. A fresh coat of paint can transform your home just in time to host with pride. Whether it’s a bold dining room accent wall, a warm neutral living room, or a fresh entryway, painting in fall ensures your home feels polished and inviting.
3. Better Indoor Air Quality with Low-VOC Paints

Modern paints are formulated to minimize fumes, but proper ventilation is still key. In the fall, you can comfortably open windows without dealing with extreme heat or cold, allowing fresh air to circulate. Choosing low-VOC (volatile organic compound) paints adds another layer of safety, making your project eco-friendly and family-friendly.
4. Budget-Friendly Timing

Since many people push painting projects to spring or summer, fall is often a slower season for painters. That means you may find better availability and scheduling flexibility. Some painting companies, like Black Pearl Painters, even offer seasonal specials to encourage homeowners to tackle projects before the year ends.

blocks.alt: fall painting, seasonal painting, interior fall painting
blocks.title: Why Fall Painting Is Perfect For Interior Painting: Tips For Homeowners

blocks.text: 5. Color Trends Perfect for Fall

Fall inspires warm, cozy tones that bring comfort indoors. Think soft taupes, creamy beiges, rich greens, or deep navy blues. These shades not only look stylish but also create a sense of warmth during darker months. Black Pearl Painters can help you choose a palette that feels timeless while still being on-trend.
6. Extending the Life of Your Paint Job

By painting in fall, you’re not just refreshing your walls for the short term—you’re also protecting them. Low humidity means less risk of moisture buildup that could affect drying and adhesion. That means your paint job will last longer, saving you time and money down the road.
7. Practical Tips for Fall Interior Painting

items: Plan ahead: Schedule your project early before the holiday rush.
Choose the right finishes: Matte for cozy bedrooms, satin for easy-to-clean kitchens, semi-gloss for trim.
Test colors in natural light: Shorter days mean lighting shifts—always check samples in both daylight and evening lighting.
Work room by room: Minimize disruption by tackling one space at a time.

blocks.text: 8. Why Work with Black Pearl Painters?

At Black Pearl Painters, we help homeowners select colors, prep surfaces, and apply paints with a professional touch that ensures lasting beauty. Our team understands the unique challenges of painting in the Northwest’s climate and knows how to achieve results that stand up to time.

From better drying conditions and holiday readiness to trendy, cozy colors, there are countless reasons to schedule your project now. Whether you want to transform one room or your entire house, Black Pearl Painters is ready to bring your vision to life this fall.

Repainting Kitchen Cabinets Surpasses Replacing

A full kitchen remodel can feel like a dream until you see the price tag. For many homeowners around Tacoma, Puyallup, and the surrounding areas, updating their kitchen without overspending is a top priority. One of the most transformative yet cost-effective ways to breathe new life into your kitchen is with cabinet painting.

At Black Pearl Painters, we specialize in turning tired, outdated kitchen cabinets into crisp, modern focal points without the mess, cost, or hassle of a full cabinet replacement. If you’re weighing your options, here’s why repainting your kitchen cabinets is the smarter choice and how our expert team delivers stunning before-and-after results that truly speak for themselves.

blocks.alt: kitchen cabinet, repainting kitchen cabinets, repaint don't replace cabinets
blocks.title: Before &Amp; After Kitchen Cabinet Painting: Why Repainting Beats Replacing

blocks.text: The High Cost of Kitchen Cabinet Replacement

Cabinet replacement often sounds appealing until homeowners dig into the logistics and expenses. Replacing cabinets involves far more than just choosing new boxes and doors. You’re also paying for demolition, disposal, new materials, installation, hardware, and often new countertops or backsplash to match the updated style. These hidden costs quickly add up, pushing most full cabinet replacements well into the five-figure range—even for smaller kitchens.

Additionally, the timeline for replacement is lengthy. It can take weeks or even months from consultation to completion, during which your kitchen may be unusable. That’s a major disruption to your daily routine.

With Black Pearl Painters, cabinet repainting typically takes just a few days, depending on the size of the job. We work efficiently and respectfully, minimizing disruption and delivering results faster than you thought possible.
Why Repainting Is the Better Alternative

If your cabinets are still structurally sound, there’s no need to tear them out. Painting is the perfect solution to refresh their appearance and update the entire look of your kitchen. Whether you want a sleek, modern white, a trendy navy blue, or a bold pop of color, painting offers virtually unlimited customization at a fraction of the cost of replacement.

Cabinet painting also allows you to preserve quality materials. Many older cabinets are made from solid wood, something rarely found in newer, budget-friendly cabinetry. Rather than replace solid, well-built cabinetry with lower-grade options, painting lets you enhance what you already have.

At Black Pearl Painters, we don’t just slap on a coat of paint. We follow a meticulous, multi-step process that includes degreasing, sanding, priming, and applying high-quality paint designed specifically for cabinetry. The result is a smooth, durable finish that resists chips, peeling, and everyday wear.
The Transformational Power of “Before and After”

Our clients are often stunned by the transformation they see when the job is complete. A kitchen that once looked dark, dated, and closed-in can be bright, fresh, and modern with just a color change. For example, one recent project in Puyallup featured honey oak cabinets straight from the early 2000s. After careful prep and a few coats of soft white satin enamel, the entire space looked larger, cleaner, and more inviting—without changing a single cabinet layout or appliance.

Another client in Tacoma opted for a two-tone look: deep forest green on the lower cabinets and warm cream above. The change added depth and personality while staying within their modest budget. The transformation went beyond visual appeal the kitchen became a space they loved to spend time in again.

These are the kinds of transformations that Black Pearl Painters is proud to deliver. We don’t just paint cabinets, we help homeowners reimagine their kitchens, all without the stress of a renovation.

blocks.alt: kitchen cabinet, repainting kitchen cabinets, repaint don't replace cabinets
blocks.title: Before &Amp; After Kitchen Cabinet Painting: Why Repainting Beats Replacing

blocks.text: It’s Not Just About Color—It’s About Craftsmanship

The biggest risk of a cabinet painting project lies in hiring the wrong contractor or trying to DIY. Cabinets require more than wall paint and a brush. Without the right prep, finish, and tools, paint can chip, flake, or bubble, leaving you with a mess and more costs to fix it later.

That’s where our experience makes all the difference. The Black Pearl Painters team is trained in cabinet-specific techniques and materials. We understand how to treat different surfaces, how to apply durable finishes, and how to create a professional look that lasts. Our attention to detail, from taping to cleanup, ensures your kitchen looks better than ever when we’re finished.
We also work closely with you to choose the right color, finish, and overall style. Whether you’re going for timeless and neutral or bold and trendy, we’ll help you bring your vision to life.
Budget-Friendly and Eco-Conscious

In addition to saving money, cabinet painting is an eco-friendlier option. Replacing cabinets means sending old materials to landfills and using new resources to manufacture replacements. Repainting, on the other hand, significantly reduces waste and makes better use of the quality products you already have.
For homeowners committed to sustainable living, this is a win-win. And because we use premium, low-VOC paints, you can feel confident about indoor air quality and safety throughout the process.
Serving Homeowners Across Tacoma, Puyallup, and Beyond

Black Pearl Painters proudly serves homeowners throughout Tacoma, Puyallup, Lakewood, University Place, and other nearby communities. We understand the local styles, trends, and expectations that homeowners have when updating their living spaces.

Our kitchen cabinet painting services are designed to be accessible, affordable, and high-impact. Whether you’re prepping to sell your home, planning a full refresh, or just want to enjoy a space that feels new again, we’ll provide professional results with a neighborly approach.
Ready for Your Kitchen’s “After”?

Don’t spend a fortune on new cabinets when a professionally painted update could achieve the same wow factor for a fraction of the cost. Let Black Pearl Painters show you just how powerful a transformation can be.
Call today to schedule a free estimate and take the first step toward a stunning kitchen you’ll love to come home to.

blocks.text: Planning to Paint Your Home? Here’s What You Need to Know First

A fresh coat of paint can do wonders for your home. It’s not just about aesthetics, but about protecting your biggest investment, increasing property value, and showing pride in where you live. For Tacoma homeowners, where damp winters and sunny summers can take a toll on siding, residential exterior painting is more than just a cosmetic update, it’s essential home maintenance.

But before you schedule your professional painters and pick out the perfect color, it’s crucial to prepare your home properly. Think of it like getting your car ready for a long road trip, you wouldn’t just hit the gas without checking the tires, topping off fluids, and packing the essentials.

In this blog, we’ll guide you step by step through how preparing and planning to paint your home in Tacoma makes the process smoother, and explain how the team at Black Pearl Painters handles all the heavy lifting so you don’t have to stress. Whether you’re painting for resale or simply refreshing your space, good prep makes all the difference.
Why Prep Matters More Than You Think

When it comes to painting the exterior of a home, prep is everything. You could use the best paint in the world, but if the surface isn’t ready, if there’s dirt, mildew, peeling paint, or hidden damage, the paint simply won’t stick or last.
Proper preparation helps ensure:

items: Fewer touch-ups and problems down the road

blocks.text: Let’s get into how to get your home ready the right way.

blocks.alt: planning to paint, preparing your property for paint
blocks.title: Planning To Paint Your Tacoma Home For A Professional Exterior Paint Job?

blocks.text: Step-by-Step Guide: How Homeowners Should Prepare for Exterior Painting
1. Clear the Perimeter
Your painters will need space to work. That means clearing the areas around your home’s exterior walls:

items: Move patio furniture, planters, garden hoses, and toys
Trim back shrubs or tree limbs that touch the house
Mow the lawn and remove any debris

blocks.text: Bonus Tip: If you’re planning to do any landscaping or outdoor projects, wait until after the painting is complete.

blocks.alt: planning to paint, preparing your property for paint
blocks.title: Planning To Paint Your Tacoma Home For A Professional Exterior Paint Job?

blocks.text: 2. Secure Your Pets
Painters will be in and out, using tools, equipment, and maybe even ladders around your property. If you have pets:

items: Keep them indoors or in a separate fenced area
Let your painters know about any pets on-site
Make sure pet access to yards and exits is restricted for safety

blocks.text: 3. Communicate Special Needs
Got a vegetable garden near the siding? Need to keep a side gate closed for security? This is the time to talk with your painters about:

items: Sensitive areas or surfaces to avoid
Access to power outlets or water
Preferred working hours or noise concerns

blocks.text: At Black Pearl Painters, our project managers will do a full walkthrough with you before the job starts, so you don’t have to worry about remembering every detail.
4. Remove Wall Hangings & Outdoor Decor
If you’ve got decorative signs, string lights, security cameras, or mounted planters on your side, take them down. These should be stored away until painting is complete.
Also, temporarily remove window screens if your painters request it (some will do this for you as part of their prep process).

blocks.alt: planning to paint, preparing your property for paint
blocks.title: Planning To Paint Your Tacoma Home For A Professional Exterior Paint Job?

blocks.text: 5. Check for Repairs

If you’ve noticed cracked trim, soft wood, or peeling caulk, let your painters know in advance. Reputable exterior house painters in Tacoma (like us!) will inspect your home for needed repairs as part of the job quote.
At Black Pearl, we even offer carpentry repair services to handle minor fixes before we paint ensuring the best foundation possible.

blocks.text: Painting in the PNW Weather: What you need to know

From drizzly mornings in Olympia to surprise heatwaves in Tacoma, the Pacific Northwest climate keeps homeowners, and their homes, on their toes. The constant cycle of rain, humidity, UV exposure, and seasonal temperature swings can wreak havoc on exterior paint. That’s why painting homes in this region isn’t just about choosing the right colors only, it’s about selecting weather-resistant paint, applying it with precision, and using techniques designed to last.

At Black Pearl Painters, we understand the unique demands of painting for rainy climates and how important it is to protect your biggest investment, your home. In this post, we’ll share the biggest challenges when painting in the PNW, the high-performance products we use to overcome them, and the expert techniques that help deliver a finish that holds up year after year.
Why the Pacific Northwest Is Tough on Paint
The PNW’s beauty is no secret, lush forests, coastal breezes, and mild summers, but that same environment is tough on exterior surfaces. Here’s why:
High Moisture Levels
Rain and humidity are part of daily life in much of Washington and Oregon. If paint isn’t properly applied or isn’t designed for damp conditions, it can:

items: Trap moisture in wood, leading to rot

blocks.text: UV Exposure
Despite our reputation for clouds, the PNW gets more than enough sunshine to degrade paint over time. UV rays break down pigments and binders, causing:
Temperature Fluctuations

Even within a single day, temperatures in the PNW can swing widely, especially in spring and fall. This leads to expansion and contraction in siding and trim materials, stressing paint films and causing premature wear.
That’s why we approach every exterior job with a plan built around durable paint finishes and application techniques designed specifically for PNW homes.

blocks.alt: Painting in the PNW, Painting Weather, Painting challenges in PNW

blocks.text: Choosing the Right Paint for the PNW Climate

The first step to a long-lasting exterior is choosing the right paint. At Black Pearl Painters, we work with industry-leading manufacturers known for their weather-resistant paint formulas, and we never compromise on product quality.
Key Features We Look For in Exterior Paint:

items: Moisture Resistance: Paints that create a strong moisture barrier without trapping water inside wood structures.
UV Protection: Formulas with fade-resistant pigments and UV blockers to protect against sun damage.
Flexibility: Coatings that can expand and contract with the substrate as temperatures change.
Mildew Resistance: Paints with antimicrobial properties to prevent black spots and surface growth.

blocks.text: We often recommend paints like Sherwin-Williams Duration, Benjamin Moore Aura, or other top-tier products specifically engineered for coastal and high-moisture regions. These paints are more expensive than bargain brands, but they last longer, look better, and save money in the long run.
Our Proven Techniques for Long-Lasting Exterior Paint Jobs

The second piece of the puzzle is how the paint is applied. Even the best product can fail without the proper prep and method. At Black Pearl Painters, our crews are trained in PNW exterior paint best practices that ensure maximum performance in our unique climate.
1. Thorough Surface Prep
This is the foundation of every great paint job. We:

items: Pressure wash all surfaces to remove dirt, mildew, and contaminants
Scrape off loose or peeling paint
Caulk gaps and cracks to block moisture intrusion
Prime bare wood, patched areas, and any glossy surfaces for adhesion

blocks.text: We don’t skip steps, and that’s why our paint jobs last.
2. Timing Is Everything
When painting in the PNW, you need to paint when conditions are just right. We schedule projects around:

items: Ample time for curing before the next rain event

blocks.text: We also use fast-drying primers and paints when needed to beat the clock and get a weather-resistant coat down in time.
3. The Right Tools and Application

We apply paint using brushes, rollers, or sprayers depending on the surface and product. Our painters use proper thicknesses (called “mils”) to ensure full coverage and a protective seal that can withstand rain, sun, and seasonal shifts.

blocks.alt: Painting in the PNW, Painting Weather, Painting challenges in PNW

blocks.text: Common Painting in the PNW Exterior Surfaces and How We Protect Them
Wood Siding & Trim
Wood is beautiful, but vulnerable to water and sun. We use penetrating primers and flexible, breathable topcoats to allow natural movement without cracking.
Stucco and Masonry
We apply elastomeric coatings that stretch with the surface and resist cracking due to expansion and contraction.
Fiber Cement and Composite Siding
These materials hold paint well but still need proper prep and top-tier paint to avoid peeling or discoloration. We use products designed for maximum adhesion and minimal maintenance.
How to Know When It’s Time to Repaint Your Home
Even a top-notch paint job won’t last forever. Watch for these signs that your home is ready for a new coat:

items: Paint is fading, chalky, or discolored
You see cracking, peeling, or bubbling
Wood siding or trim is soft or spongy
Mildew or mold is visible on paint surfaces
Your home just looks tired or dated

blocks.text: Most homes in the PNW need repainting every 5–8 years depending on sun exposure, materials, and prior prep.

We’ve painted hundreds of homes across the Puget Sound and beyond—and we know what works. Our process is designed to handle the region’s rain, moisture, and UV exposure, and we’re proud to stand behind our work.
With Black Pearl Painters, you get:

Expert consultation on the right paints and finishes for your specific locationThorough preparation and attention to weather timingHigh-quality products tailored to Northwest conditionsLong-lasting protection with clean, beautiful resultsA team of professionals who care about craftsmanship and curb appeal

blocks.text: Pressure Washing Prep: A Q&A Guide from Black Pearl Painters

Maintaining your home’s exterior in Puget Sound’s damp, moss-friendly climate requires more than just good paint, it demands thoughtful preparation, and that starts with professional pressure washing. At Black Pearl Painters, we often hear the question:
“Do I really need pressure washing before a paint job?”
The short answer? Yes, especially in Western Washington, where wet seasons, algae, and wind-blown debris are constant threats to your paint’s performance.

In this blog post, we break down everything homeowners in Tacoma, Bonney Lake, Puyallup, and beyond need to know about how power washing prep plays a critical role in prolonging the life of exterior paint.
Q: What exactly is pressure washing in the context of exterior painting?

A: Pressure washing (sometimes called power washing) is the use of high-pressure water jets to remove dirt, mold, mildew, loose paint, pollen, and other contaminants from your home’s exterior surfaces. It’s one of the first steps in a proper paint preparation process.

Before we ever open a paint can, Black Pearl Painters carefully evaluates your siding and surfaces, then performs a thorough, professional pressure wash to ensure we’re painting on a clean, solid foundation.
Q: Why is pressure washing so important before painting?
A: Paint doesn’t just stick to your home, it adheres to whatever is on your home. That could be:

If those contaminants remain, your new paint won’t bond properly, leading to early peeling, bubbling, cracking, and fading. A clean, pressure-washed surface gives your new coat of paint the best chance at maximum durability and weather resistance.

blocks.alt: pressure washing, exterior pressure washing, pressure wash home
blocks.title: Pressure Washing Prep: How It Extends Exterior Paint Life In Puget Sound

blocks.text: Q: How does Puget Sound’s climate affect exterior paint?
A: Puget Sound’s combination of heavy rainfall, coastal moisture, and shade-loving moss makes homes especially vulnerable to:
If these issues aren’t addressed before repainting, your new paint can trap moisture beneath it, leading to early paint failure and even wood rot.
Pressure washing eliminates the mold, mildew, and grime at the root—making it one of the best long-term investments in your home’s protective finish.
Q: Will pressure washing damage my siding or windows?
A: Not when it’s done by professionals like Black Pearl Painters. Our experienced crew uses the right level of pressure for your home’s material—whether it’s:
We also avoid vulnerable areas like window seals, electrical fixtures, and roof flashing. Our approach is gentle where it needs to be, yet powerful enough to lift years of dirt and growth.
Q: Can I just use a garden hose or do it myself?
A: A garden hose won’t remove the deeply embedded grime, mildew spores, or chalky residue needed to properly prep for painting.
DIY pressure washing also carries risks, including:

items: Damaging siding or trim with too much pressure
Driving water under siding or into attic vents
Leaving uneven cleaning patterns or missing key areas

blocks.text: That’s why we always recommend professional pressure washing as part of a complete painting prep process. It ensures your surface is clean, dry, and ready to accept a long-lasting coat of paint.
Q: How long after pressure washing can you paint?
A: Timing is important. We typically allow 1–3 days of drying time, depending on:

items: Siding material (wood takes longer to dry than vinyl)

blocks.text: In Puget Sound, we plan around the forecast and ensure siding is 100% dry before painting begins. Painting too soon after washing can trap moisture under the paint, leading to bubbling and mildew growth.
Q: How often should I pressure wash my home?
A: Even if you’re not painting, we recommend pressure washing your home every 1–2 years to keep siding in good condition, especially in Bonney Lake, Tacoma, and other damp regions.
Routine cleaning:

items: Preserves your paint’s color and finish
Protects your siding from premature wear

blocks.text: Think of it as a cost-effective way to extend the life of your last paint job while prepping for the next one.
Q: What other prep steps follow pressure washing?
A: At Black Pearl Painters, pressure washing is just one part of our comprehensive paint prep system. After the wash, we:

items: Inspect for damage – looking for cracked siding, rotten wood, or loose trim
Caulk and seal gaps – to protect your home from water intrusion
Scrape and sand – any peeling paint or rough patches
Prime bare wood – to ensure adhesion and color uniformity

blocks.text: Together, these steps lay the groundwork for a professional-grade finish that lasts for years, even in Puget Sound’s wet, wild weather.
Q: What does pressure washing cost in Puget Sound?

A: When bundled with an exterior paint project, pressure washing is included in our estimate. On its own, a professional house pressure washing service typically ranges from $200–$500, depending on the home’s size and condition.
That said, skipping this step can cost you much more in early paint failure and repairs. A clean home = a longer-lasting paint job.
Q: Can pressure washing help with resale or curb appeal?
A: Absolutely! Even without painting, a thorough pressure wash can:

items: Remove unsightly stains and green moss
Make your home look newer and well-maintained
Add value if you’re preparing to sell

blocks.text: For real estate agents and home stagers, a clean exterior can make or break a buyer’s first impression.

blocks.text: Why Curb Appeal Matters for Boosting Home Value

When it comes to increasing your home’s value and making a lasting first impression, nothing has a greater visual impact for the cost than a fresh coat of paint. Whether you’re preparing to list your property or simply want to fall in love with your home all over again, curb appeal painting is one of the smartest and most effective upgrades you can make, especially during the summer months.

At Black Pearl Painters, we help Pacific Northwest homeowners turn faded, weathered exteriors into polished showpieces. With expert guidance, the right products, and a strategic approach, exterior paint can do more than make your home look good, it can increase home value, boost buyer interest, and protect your investment for years to come.
Let’s look at why painting in the summer is the perfect time to maximize curb appeal of your home or business, plus tips and inspiration to get the most out of your paint project.
Why Curb Appeal Matters More Than Ever

Whether you’re thinking of selling soon or staying put, curb appeal plays a critical role in how your home is perceived. In fact, real estate experts consistently rank exterior updates, especially painting, as one of the highest return investments homeowners can make.
According to recent data:

items: A well-done exterior paint job can yield a return on investment (ROI) of up to 55–100%.

First impressions are formed in seconds, and a freshly painted home immediately communicates that it’s well cared for.

blocks.text: Why Summer Is Prime Time for Exterior Painting
For homeowners in the Pacific Northwest, summer offers ideal conditions for exterior painting:

With less rain and moisture in the forecast, painters can work efficiently with fewer delays.

Top Exterior Paint Tips to Increase Home Value

1. Choose Timeless, Broad-Appeal Colors

If you’re painting with resale in mind, choose colors that appeal to a wide range of buyers. Neutral, earthy tones and soft grays or blues are especially popular. For trim and accents, crisp white or charcoal creates clean contrast and sophistication.

2. Update More Than Just the Siding

items: The front door (go bold for contrast!)

Professional curb appeal painting always starts with solid prep. That means:

4. Highlight Architectural Features
Use paint to enhance the beauty of your home’s architecture. A second accent color on dormers, eaves, or decorative trim can add depth and character without overwhelming the exterior.
5. Coordinate with Your Landscape
Choose colors that complement your home’s environment. Greenery, brickwork, stone features, or garden beds should harmonize with your paint palette; not clash with it.

blocks.text: Paint Sheens: How to Choose the Right Finish

Choosing a paint color is the fun part, but picking the right finish is where many homeowners get stuck. Sheen, or the level of gloss in your paint, plays a huge role in both the look and performance of your walls. Whether you’re painting a cozy bedroom or a busy hallway, the right paint sheen can enhance aesthetics, improve durability, and make cleaning easier.

At Black Pearl Painters, we don’t just help our Pacific Northwest clients choose the perfect colors, we guide them through the best paint types for every room, based on traffic, lighting, and style preferences. In this post, we’ll walk you through a complete paint sheens guide so you can feel confident in your choices, and enjoy long-lasting, beautiful results.
What are Paint Sheens, Exactly?

Paint sheens refers to how shiny or reflective the surface is once the paint dries. Higher sheen paints have more gloss and reflect more light. Lower sheen paints have a more matte, velvety look and absorb more light.
Your choice affects:

items: How the color appears in different lighting
How easy it is to clean
How well imperfections are hidden or revealed
The overall vibe and style of a room

blocks.text: Let’s break down the main types of sheen, from ultra-flat to super-shiny, and when and where to use them.
1. Flat or Matte Finish
Best for:

items: Rooms with lots of wall imperfections

blocks.text: Flat and matte paints have little to no sheen, giving them a smooth, elegant look that’s perfect for spaces where you want a calm, cozy atmosphere. They’re excellent at hiding surface flaws, like small cracks or uneven textures, making them ideal for older homes or ceilings with visible seams.

However, flat paint is the least washable of all sheens. It can scuff and mark more easily, so it’s not the best choice for high-traffic areas or homes with pets and kids, unless you don’t mind frequent touch-ups.
2. Eggshell Finish
Best for:

Eggshell is one of the most popular finishes, and for good reason. It has just a touch of sheen, offering a nice balance between flat and glossy. It’s more durable and washable than matte, but still soft enough to keep walls looking smooth and rich.
Why we love it: Eggshell gives walls a warm, inviting glow while offering some stain resistance. It works beautifully in spaces that see regular, but not rough, use.
3. Satin Finish
Best for:

Satin is a step up in shine and cleanability, making it a great option for moisture-prone or high-traffic spaces. It resists mildew and stands up well to scrubbing; perfect for busy households or areas that need regular wipe-downs.

It reflects more light than eggshell, which adds brightness to darker rooms. Just be aware: satin finishes can slightly highlight surface imperfections, so great prep work is key; something Black Pearl Painters always provides.
4. Semi-Gloss Finish
Best for:

items: Bathrooms and kitchens (for a little extra shine)

blocks.text: Semi-gloss is durable, moisture-resistant, and very easy to clean. It’s a top choice for areas that get touched or bumped frequently, like baseboards, door frames, and cabinet doors.

It has a noticeable sheen, so it will draw attention to the areas it covers. That makes it ideal for architectural details you want to highlight, but less ideal for rough or uneven surfaces unless they’ve been smoothed out properly.

blocks.alt: paint sheens, paint finishes, painting sheens and finishes
blocks.title: Paint Sheens: Choosing The Right Finish For Every Room

blocks.text: 5. Gloss (or High-Gloss) Finish
Best for:

High-gloss is the most reflective finish, and the most durable. It creates a glass-like sheen that’s dramatic and sleek, perfect for a bold modern look. It’s not widely used on walls but can be striking on built-ins, stair railings, or as a statement trim in a high-style space.
That said, it will magnify any surface imperfection, so proper sanding and priming are essential.
Quick Sheen Comparison Chart
How to Choose the Right Sheen for Each Room
Still unsure? Here’s a room-by-room breakdown using Black Pearl’s go-to recommendations:
Living Room:

items: Eggshell gives warmth and hides minor imperfections. Satin adds cleanability if you have kids or pets.

blocks.text: Dining Room:

items: Adds a touch of elegance without too much shine.

blocks.text: Bedrooms:

items: Use matte for a luxurious, cozy feel or eggshell for a little more durability.

blocks.text: Bathrooms:

items: Satin is moisture-resistant; semi-gloss adds extra protection in humid conditions.

blocks.text: Kitchen:

items: Both stand up well to grease, moisture, and frequent cleaning.

blocks.text: Trim, Doors & Cabinets:
Ceilings:

items: Hides flaws and creates a soft background for your space.

blocks.text: Why Finish Matters as Much as Color

At Black Pearl Painters, we often tell clients: The right finish is just as important as the right shade. You could pick the perfect color, but if the sheen doesn’t match the room’s function, you’ll end up with issues like:

Our team takes the time to understand your lifestyle, lighting conditions, and design preferences to recommend the best paint finish for walls, ceilings, and everything in between. We don’t just paint homes; we enhance them with professional expertise and long-term thinking.
Let Sheen Work in Your Favor

Paint isn’t one-size-fits-all. Whether you’re refreshing your whole home or updating a single room, understanding the differences between matte, eggshell, satin, semi-gloss, and gloss can help you make smarter choices that look great and last longer.

blocks.text: How Paint Color and Finish Can Make Your Room Seem Bigger

When square footage is limited, creativity becomes your best tool, and one of the most effective (and affordable) ways to transform a small space is with paint. Whether you’re living in a cozy condo, a compact townhome, or you’re simply looking to make a tight room feel more open, the right color and finish can dramatically change how a space looks and feels.

At Black Pearl Painters, we help Pacific Northwest homeowners unlock their home’s full potential, no matter the size. In this post, we’ll share our favorite painting tips for small rooms, including clever color tricks, the best finishes to use, and how to use paint to create the illusion of space, light, and height. If you’re looking for a low-cost upgrade that delivers big impact, this is for you.
The Power of Paint Color and Finish in Small Rooms

Unlike major renovations, painting is quick, cost-effective, and incredibly transformative. But in small rooms, the impact goes beyond color, paint can influence how the space is perceived in terms of depth, light, and even function.
With smart choices, you can:

items: Bounce more light around the room
Create a more cohesive and calming environment

blocks.text: Let’s break down the techniques professional painters and designers use to make small rooms feel bigger.

blocks.alt: paint color and finish, painting small spaces tips
blocks.title: How Paint Color And Finish Helps Small Spaces

blocks.text: 1. Choose Light, Airy Colors to Open Up a Room
It’s no secret: light colors make a space feel larger. They reflect more light than dark tones, helping walls recede and giving the room a more open, expansive feel.
Best Paint Colors for Small Spaces:

items: Soft whites and off-whites: Clean, classic, and versatile.
Light grays and greiges: Add subtle contrast without making the room feel enclosed.
Pale blues, greens, and lavenders: Cool tones visually push walls back, especially when paired with natural light.

blocks.text: Pro tip: Paint the walls, ceiling, and trim in slightly varied shades of the same color to create a seamless look that makes boundaries between surfaces less noticeable.
2. Use Satin or Eggshell Finishes to Reflect Light

In small rooms, the right paint finish is just as important as color. Matte finishes absorb light, which can make walls feel flat or dull in tight spaces. On the other hand, satin and eggshell finishes reflect light gently, enhancing brightness and making surfaces feel more dynamic.
At Black Pearl Painters, we often recommend:

items: Satin for walls in living rooms, hallways, and bedrooms (durable + reflective)
Eggshell for low-traffic areas or ceilings with a subtle glow
Semi-gloss or high-gloss for trim, doors, and cabinetry to define edges and add dimension

blocks.text: Bonus: These finishes are also easier to clean, especially important in smaller homes where space gets used more intensively.
3. Paint Ceilings a Lighter Shade to Create Height
Many small rooms suffer from low ceilings or boxy proportions. One easy trick? Paint the ceiling a lighter shade than the walls, or even the same color, but in a flat or low-sheen finish.
This draws the eye upward and creates the illusion of height, especially when combined with vertically oriented design elements like tall bookshelves or vertical trim.
Feeling bold? A glossy white ceiling can make light bounce dramatically and feel like a skylight, even if the room doesn’t have one.
4. Use Accent Walls to Add Depth Without Clutter

While all-white rooms can feel spacious, they can also feel bland. A well-placed accent wall adds depth and personality without crowding the space. The key is choosing the right wall and the right color.
Accent Wall Ideas for Small Rooms:

items: Deeper tone of the main color: Soft gray with a charcoal accent
Moody blue or green: Especially behind a headboard or focal furniture
Geometric or color-block designs: Adds interest without relying on artwork or décor

blocks.text: In small open-concept homes or condos, accent walls can help define separate areas, like a dining nook or office zone, without building physical walls.
5. Extend Color Across Surfaces for Continuity

One advanced trick used by designers and professional painters is to carry paint color and finish across walls, baseboards, trim, and sometimes even ceilings. This monochromatic look removes visual breaks and gives the impression of more continuous space.
Especially effective in:
Choose a soft neutral and paint everything, from crown molding to door frames, in the same or similar shade. The result? Clean, minimal, and incredibly modern.
6. Match Paint Color and Finish Choices to Your Natural Light
Not all small rooms are created equal, some may be naturally bright, while others are dark or windowless. Paint can help balance out these light levels.

items: North-facing rooms (cool light): Warm neutrals and soft creams keep the room cozy.
South-facing rooms (warm light): Cool grays, blues, and greens help balance out the brightness.
Low-light rooms: Use semi-gloss or satin finishes to reflect what little light there is and avoid dark, flat shades.

blocks.text: If you’re unsure, Black Pearl Painters offers in-home color consultations to help you choose the best shades for your lighting conditions and goals.
Before-and-After Inspiration: Small Space, Big Impact

Tiny Bedroom RefreshA condo owner in Seattle wanted to make her 10×10 bedroom feel less cramped. We painted the walls and ceiling a soft mist gray in eggshell finish and added a powder blue accent behind the bed. Satin white trim gave the room clean lines and a pop of contrast. The result? A cozy but visually spacious retreat.

Windowless Laundry Nook MakeoverWe took a dark, cave-like laundry closet in Tacoma and painted the walls and ceiling in a warm linen white. Satin finish paint helped reflect the artificial lighting, making the space feel fresh and inviting.

When every inch counts, there’s no room for error. Uneven lines, poor lighting, or cheap paint can ruin the feel of a small space fast. That’s why homeowners across the Pacific Northwest trust Black Pearl Painters.

We bring:Expert knowledge of color psychology and space-enhancing techniquesSmooth, clean application for crisp lines and long-lasting resultsHigh-quality, low-VOC paints perfect for indoor useFast, respectful service that minimizes disruption in small homes or shared spaces

Black Pearl Painters prioritizes thorough preparation, including surface repairs, priming, and precision painting, to prevent damage and extend the life of your home’s exterior and interior walls.

A fresh interior paint job does more than refresh your space, it also improves indoor air quality. Older paints may contain volatile organic compounds (VOCs) that release harmful fumes over time. Did you know that the right paint choices can improve your home’s energy efficiency? Painting your condo or townhome is a great way to refresh its look, protect your investment, and increase curb appeal. But before you break out the color swatches and paint samples, there’s one major hurdle to clear: your Homeowners Association (COA/TOA/HOA). Unlike standalone homes, condos and townhomes typically fall under strict COA/TOA/HOA painting rules that dictate everything from color palettes to scheduling and even the types of finishes allowed.

Navigating these COA/TOA/HOA regulations can feel overwhelming, especially if you’re hoping to start your project soon. That’s where hiring seasoned professionals like Black Pearl Painters can turn a potentially frustrating experience into a smooth, stress-free success.

blocks.text: Home Restorations: Preserve Character. Add Longevity. Paint the Right Way.

Craftsman homes are among the most cherished architectural styles in the Pacific Northwest. With their overhanging eaves, tapered columns, wood siding, and historic charm, these homes speak to another era—one of thoughtful design and enduring quality.
But if you own a Craftsman or older home in Tacoma, Bonney Lake, or surrounding Puget Sound neighborhoods, maintaining that character often comes down to how you prep and paint.

At Black Pearl Painters, we specialize in older home restoration painting, with a strong emphasis on proper prep, surface repair, and historic color matching. Whether your home dates to the early 1900s or just reflects a classic Craftsman style, this guide will help you understand the essential steps for a lasting, beautiful finish.
Why Painting Older Homes Requires a Different Approach

Unlike modern construction, older homes come with unique challenges: aged wood, lead-based paint, multiple layers of coatings, and intricate architectural details. Painting over these without the right prep not only risks peeling and failure, but it can also damage the home’s historic value.
Craftsman homes often include:

items: Wood lap siding or cedar shingles

blocks.text: Each of these elements needs careful attention before paint is applied. Quick, modern methods simply don’t cut it.
Step 1: Inspection and Surface Assessment
Every successful older home restorations and painting project starts with a full inspection of the exterior. At Black Pearl Painters, we examine:

items: Wood condition – checking for rot, warping, or insect damage
Previous coatings – identifying flaking, chipping, or incompatible layers
Moisture damage – especially in rooflines, eaves, and near ground contact
Lead paint risks – for homes built before 1978, lead-safe practices are required

blocks.text: Failing to inspect these issues can cause even premium paints to fail prematurely.
Step 2: Professional Paint Prep for Historic Exteriors

Proper paint prep for Craftsman homes is labor-intensive but essential for long-term results. Unlike newer builds that may only need a light wash and scuff, older home restorations require several key steps:
Power Washing (Low-Pressure for Delicate Areas)
We start by cleaning the surface to remove mildew, dirt, and loose material. On delicate trim or weathered siding, we may use low-pressure washing or even hand washing to avoid water intrusion.
Paint Removal & Scraping

Where peeling is severe or multiple layers exist, hand scraping and sanding are used to feather edges and smooth the surface. In cases of lead-based paint, EPA-certified containment and disposal procedures are followed.
Surface Repairs & Carpentry
Rotten trim, cracked siding, or missing shingles? We offer on-site carpentry repair to replace damaged wood with matching profiles. This prevents future decay and restores original details.
Caulking & Sealing
Gaps around windows, doors, and trim are filled with high-quality exterior caulk, creating a weathertight seal that enhances both appearance and performance.

blocks.alt: home restorations, older home restoration, craftsman home restorations
blocks.title: Older Home Restorations: Paint Prep &Amp; Color Matching For Craftsman Homes

blocks.text: Step 3: Primer Selection for Aged Wood
Older wood can be dry, porous, and full of tanning, especially if it’s redwood or cedar. That’s why primer selection is critical.

items: Oil-based primers often work best for bare wood or areas previously painted with oil
Stain-blocking primers prevent bleed-through from water stains, tannins, or rust
Bonding primers ensure proper adhesion on slick or chalky surfaces

blocks.text: We always tailor the primer to the surface, especially important when dealing with multiple surfaces like lap siding, vertical board, soffits, and fascia.
Step 4: Color Matching for Craftsman Charm

One of the most important, and often stressful, parts of painting an older home is choosing the right color palette. Craftsman homes are known for their earth-toned hues, inspired by nature and the Arts & Crafts movement.
Popular Craftsman Color Palettes:

items: Forest green with cream and burgundy trim
Olive or sage with rust-red and tan accents
Charcoal with pale gray and rich wood-tone highlights

blocks.text: At Black Pearl Painters, we help you either match the original paint scheme (through color matching tools or historic records) or create an updated palette that respects the home’s heritage.
We use Sherwin-Williams historic color collections and digital mockups to preview your choices before painting begins.
Step 5: Choosing the Right Paint
For older homes in the damp Puget Sound climate, durability matters just as much as aesthetics.
We recommend Sherwin-Williams Duration® or Emerald® exterior paints, which offer:

items: Exceptional adhesion on older, textured surfaces
Flexible film that moves with expanding and contracting wood

blocks.text: These high-performance paints ensure your home stays protected for years to come, while showcasing its original beauty.
Step 6: The Craft of Application
Vintage homes deserve a craftsman’s touch; not a rushed spray job. Depending on the surface, we use:

items: Back-brushing techniques to work paint into textured or porous wood
Hand-painting on trim and details for clean, crisp edges
Controlled spray and roll combos where appropriate for efficiency without sacrificing coverage

blocks.text: The result is a cohesive, professionally restored exterior that maintains the home’s identity while protecting it for decades.

items: Skilled surface prep and woodwork repair

blocks.text: What Are VOCs and Why Should You Care?

VOCs, or volatile organic compounds, are chemicals that easily evaporate at room temperature and are commonly found in traditional paints, solvents, and finishes. When paint containing high VOC levels is applied, it releases these compounds into the air, often resulting in:
For families, especially those with young children, elderly residents, or individuals with respiratory conditions, minimizing VOC exposure is critical.
The Benefits of Low VOC & Eco-Friendly Paints
Choosing low VOC or zero VOC paints for your Bonney Lake home offers several benefits beyond environmental friendliness:
1. Improved Indoor Air Quality
Low VOC paints significantly reduce off-gassing, making the air inside your home cleaner and safer to breathe especially important during winter months when windows stay closed.
2. Faster Re-Entry Time
With less odor and fewer irritants, rooms painted with eco-friendly products can often be safely occupied sooner ideal for families who need to keep their routines moving.
3. Lower Environmental Impact
Eco-conscious paints contain fewer harmful ingredients and are often manufactured with sustainability in mind, including recyclable packaging and reduced emissions during production.
4. High Performance and Durability
Gone are the days when green products meant sacrificing quality. Today’s low VOC paints, especially those from Sherwin-Williams, offer exceptional coverage, durability, and color retention.

Interior vs. Exterior: Eco-Friendly Considerations
Interior Painting in Bonney Lake

Indoor projects are where low VOC and zero VOC paints matter most. Since the paint stays enclosed inside your living space, it’s crucial to select safe products. We prioritize Harmony® or Emerald® lines for interior rooms where your family spends the most time.

Choosing the Right Finish for Eco Paints
Eco-friendly paints come in a variety of sheens and finishes, including:

items: Matte or Flat: Great for ceilings and low-traffic walls

Tips for an Eco-Conscious Paint Project

Reuse drop cloths and trays when possible or choose biodegradable alternatives.

blocks.text: Surface Prep Can Make Your Paint Job Easier

When most people imagine a fresh paint job, their minds jump straight to the final coat—the sleek finish, the perfect color, the transformative effect. But what truly makes or breaks that picture-perfect result happens before the first drop of paint ever hits the wall. It’s the surface preparation, the often-overlooked foundation of professional painting, that determines whether your paint job will look good and stay looking good.

At Black Pearl Painters, we believe that a quality paint job begins long before the brush comes out of the bucket. We’re proud to be known for our meticulous surface preparation for painting, a critical part of our process that sets us apart from DIY attempts and budget-level paint crews.
Let’s take a deeper look at why proper painting prep work is essential for a lasting paint finish, and how Black Pearl Painters ensures your home or business gets the care it truly deserves.
The Hidden Power of Painting Prep Work

You wouldn’t build a house without first laying a strong foundation. In the same way, you shouldn’t paint a surface without properly preparing it first. Skipping or rushing this crucial step is one of the biggest reasons paint fails prematurely; think peeling, cracking, bubbling, or fading within months instead of years.

Proper painting prep work includes several steps, each designed to address common issues that can interfere with paint adhesion or appearance. At Black Pearl Painters, we treat this phase with the same level of precision and care as the painting itself.

blocks.alt: surface prep, painting prep, surface preparation
blocks.title: Beyond The Brush: Why Surface Prep Makes Or Breaks Your Paint Job

blocks.text: Key Steps in Surface Preparation for Painting
Here’s a breakdown of the essential prep work our professional painters complete before the brush or roller even comes out:
1. Cleaning the Surface

Whether it’s interior walls, trim, or the exterior of a home, all surfaces collect dust, grime, mildew, and grease over time. We start by thoroughly cleaning everything. This might mean power washing siding, wiping down walls, or using specialty cleaners to remove contaminants.
Why it matters: Paint won’t properly adhere to a dirty surface. Cleaning ensures we’re working on a blank canvas—not one covered in residue.
2. Sanding for Smoothness and Adhesion

Rough patches, old paint drips, and glossy finishes all need to be smoothed out before painting. Our painters sand surfaces not just for aesthetics, but to create the right texture for new paint to grip.
Why it matters: Sanding eliminates imperfections and helps paint bond evenly, reducing the chance of peeling and giving you a smoother, more attractive result.
3. Scraping Away Loose Paint
If existing paint is flaking or chipping, we scrape it away. This is especially important in older homes, where paint might be failing due to moisture or age.
Why it matters: Painting over compromised areas will only accelerate further peeling. Removing unstable paint creates a stable base for fresh coats.
4. Caulking Gaps and Cracks
One of the most overlooked parts of prep work is caulking. Our team inspects trim, siding, window frames, and baseboards for gaps or cracks, which we fill with high-quality caulk.
Why it matters: Caulking prevents moisture intrusion and air leaks, both of which can damage paint and the structure beneath. It also creates a more polished, seamless look.
5. Patching and Repairing Surfaces
Dings, dents, nail holes, and damaged drywall or wood all need attention before painting. We use spackle, wood filler, or epoxy as needed to restore surfaces.
Why it matters: A fresh coat of paint can’t hide damage; it can highlight it. Fixing issues first results in a flawless finish.
6. Priming with Purpose
Finally, we apply primer to surfaces that need it, such as bare wood, patched areas, or previously stained walls.
Why it matters: Primer helps paint adhere better, provides a consistent surface for color application, and prevents stains from bleeding through. It’s your insurance policy for a durable, even coat.

blocks.alt: surface prep, painting prep, surface preparation
blocks.title: Beyond The Brush: Why Surface Prep Makes Or Breaks Your Paint Job

blocks.text: What Happens Without Proper Surface Prep?
Homeowners who take the DIY route, or hire painters who cut corners to save time or money—often skip crucial prep steps. Unfortunately, this shortcut comes at a cost.

items: Premature peeling or bubbling: If the surface wasn’t cleaned or sanded correctly.
Visible flaws and texture issues: If dents and holes weren’t repaired.
Uneven color and sheen: If primer wasn’t used where needed.
Repainting sooner than expected: If paint fails due to poor adhesion.

We’ve seen firsthand how proper surface preparation for painting makes all the difference. That’s why we train our teams to approach every job, from a single room to a full exterior, with a focus on detail, durability, and excellence.
Here’s what you get when you work with us:

items: Expert assessment: We evaluate your surfaces thoroughly before starting and build a prep plan tailored to your home’s condition.
Top-tier materials: We use professional-grade caulks, fillers, and primers to create a superior foundation.
Experienced craftsmen: Our painters are skilled not just in brushing and rolling, but in everything that comes before.
Long-lasting results: When paint is applied to a properly prepped surface, it performs better and lasts longer, saving you money and time in the long run.

blocks.text: Our clients regularly tell us they’re amazed at the transformation and how well their paint jobs hold up over time. That’s not just luck. That’s Black Pearl precision.
Prep Like a Pro for Results That Last

A stunning paint job doesn’t start with a color swatch. It starts with surface prep. At Black Pearl Painters, we understand that taking the time to do it right makes all the difference in the final result. While DIYers and budget crews may skimp on prep to save time or money, we invest the effort up front to ensure our clients enjoy a lasting paint finish they can be proud of for years to come.

blocks.text: Why Exterior Color Matters for Condos and Townhomes

Your home’s exterior is the first thing people see and for condos and townhomes, which often share walls or uniform design elements, it’s essential that colors complement both the architecture and the community.
Here’s why making the right choice matters:

items: Curb Appeal: Fresh, modern color can make your unit look new again.
Resale Value: Homes with attractive, on-trend colors often sell faster and for more.
Community Cohesion: Colors should harmonize with neighboring units while still offering individuality.
COA/TOA/COA/TOA/HOA Requirements: Most communities have rules regarding paint colors—some even provide approved palettes.

blocks.text: Step-by-Step: How to Choose the Best Exterior Paint Colors
Here’s a clear process to make your paint color decision smooth, COA/TOA/COA/TOA/HOA-compliant, and stress-free.
Step 1: Check COA/TOA/COA/TOA/HOA Guidelines
Start by requesting your COA/TOA/COA/TOA/HOA’s approved color list. Some associations allow homeowner proposals, but most will have a limited palette for exterior painting.
Step 2: Evaluate Your Architecture and Materials

Is your condo or townhome modern, colonial, craftsman, or mid-century? Your home’s architectural style should guide your palette. Also consider any brick, stone, or siding features that won’t be painted.
Step 3: Consider Tacoma’s Climate and Lighting
Lighting varies greatly depending on your location. Tacoma’s cloudy skies and evergreen surroundings can mute or enhance certain tones. Test swatches in morning and afternoon light before deciding.
Step 4: Test Paint Samples on the Actual Surface
Paint a few swatches directly onto your exterior walls. View them at different times of day, especially in Tacoma’s often overcast conditions.
Step 5: Coordinate with Neighboring Units
If you’re in a connected building or row of townhomes, avoid selecting the same exact color as your neighbor. Choose a coordinating but distinct tone to preserve visual interest.
Step 6: Submit Your Color Selection for COA/TOA/COA/TOA/HOA Approval
Even if you’re choosing from the approved palette, always submit your choices to avoid delays or costly repaints. We can help with digital mock-ups or formal proposals as needed.
Our Favorite COA/TOA/COA/TOA/HOA-Compliant Color Combinations for 2025
If you’re overwhelmed by the choices, here are three safe and stylish color combinations that work well for Tacoma condos and townhomes exterior painting:
1. Alabaster (SW 7008) with Urbane Bronze (SW 7048) Trim
Classic yet bold. Great for traditional buildings with large eaves or trim.
2. Dorian Gray (SW 7017) with Snowbound (SW 7004) Accents
A refined neutral combo with subtle contrast and modern appeal.
3. Evergreen Fog (SW 9130) with Shoji White (SW 7042) Trim
Nature-inspired, soft and sophisticated; perfect for Northwest aesthetics.

Bedrooms and living areas can take on bolder hues like Persimmon or Silvermist for warmth and personality.
